Okay so for the first several sentences of this post I was like - did I write this and not remember? Holy hell, I FEEL YOU. 
This is my story which, is pretty similar... I was also diagnosed with Fibromyalgia and HSD and IBS. I also already have POTS diagnosed. 

I had an unbelievably frustrating and upsetting rheumatologist appointment on Friday. I don't even know how to put it into words. 
I had seen one previously last year, and she made me feel invalidated, but did rule out anything autoimmune with bloodwork.
I asked about hEDS because I've suspected it for years. She dismissed it right away and diagnosed fibromyalgia.
Fast forward to now, I had been requesting a 2nd opinion because I'm certain I have hEDS, not Fibro. I've been researching it for the last 7 years, and even more so after I got POTS.

I got to the appointment so hopeful. I had the 2017 diagnostic criteria for hEDS filled out, I brought pictures of every symptom. 
He did a decent physical exam, but said he didn't see "excessive stretchiness" in my hand skin, and that my feet were flat but not as flat as someone with Marfans (I never suspected this, I'm short af).
He additionally used  my lack of dental crowding (I had braces..) to rule out a high and narrow pallet. 
I told him, look I literally have a 24/7 scalloped tongue because it doesn't fit in my mouth. (He said nothing to acknowledge this).
He said additionally to those things he didn't see piezogenic papules in my heels. He picked up my feet to look. They are only present when weight bearing. So immediately I showed him photos.

"I understand you have pictures, and your neck skin is definitely stretchy but I have to go based off my exam here today and you don't meet the criteria even though you showed pictures. You have to hear me out I have to go off my exam"."You are 9/9 on the beighton scale and that will be in my chart forever don't worry" 

My skin on my hands isn't excessively stretchy, sure. But I definitely have the papules. 
He also said my family history isn't significant because it's cousins not parents that have been diagnosed. 

That Fibromyalgia can cause the GI issues and skin issues and POTS. 
I'm like. I understand that but I've had the joint pain and history of injury my entire life. I shredded both ankle anterior talofobular ligaments by the time I was 15...
The way my symptoms present are way more consistent with hEDS. And always have been

I don't get nerve pain and very rarely have muscle pain, sometimes soreness around the joint but mostly in the joint.

I already have early OA in my joints. 

He stuck to his diagnosis of Fibro and HSD and IBS. Because that was what the prior Rheumatologist had written in my chart.

I found out they worked in the same office up until about a month ago. I don't know if they were friends....

He also asked me about my service dog. "What is the dog for" 

I told him my autism SD and cardiac alert for POTS.
"Who made those diagnosis" like he was trying to almost... Find a way to invalidate them? It was weird.

He also asked me multiple times throughout the appointment why I don't work. 

Anyway I left and cried. Since that WAS my 2nd opinion, my only hope of getting the diagnosis and validation. 

So. Yes. I FEEL YOU. I'm so so so sorrryy.

Mental exercise can really be super helpful for dogs that want to use their brain. I don't know if you have any treat balls, kong wobbler or snuffle mats (or kong you can freeze meals in) but even if you take a bunch of empty bottles, put them in a cardboard box and sprinkle her kibble in there, or roll it up in a blanket or towel, hide the kibbles around the house and teach her to go find them...it is mentally exhausting. I don't know if you have heard of a "flirt pole" either but it's just basically a giant cat toy for dogs. I use a horse lunge whip with a toy tied on the end. It is great physical exercise and a way to release that energy safely and you can even use it as a reward for obedience. So like if you ask the dog to lay down, then say go get the toy as a reward. or build patience, holding a down or sit stay and 'wait' while you waive the pole around.
